name: Phishing to Data Exfiltration
description: Classic spear-phishing attack chain leading to data exfiltration via credential theft and privilege escalation.
text: A phishing email was sent containing a malicious link. The victim clicked the link which led to credential theft via a fake login form. The attacker used stolen credentials to log in, escalated privileges to admin, accessed sensitive data, and exfiltrated it through an encrypted tunnel.

name: Brute Force to Lateral Movement
description: Brute-force attack on exposed service leading to lateral movement across the network.
text: An attacker performed a port scan to identify open services, followed by brute force authentication attempts. After successfully logging in, the attacker moved laterally across the network, escalated privileges, and accessed sensitive data.

name: Insider Threat Data Theft
description: Malicious insider accessing and exfiltrating sensitive data using legitimate credentials.
text: An insider logged in using legitimate credentials during off-hours, accessed files outside their normal scope, downloaded large volumes of data, and exfiltrated it to an external destination.

name: Ransomware Deployment Chain
description: Multi-stage ransomware attack from initial access to encryption and ransom demand.
text: A phishing email delivered a malware payload. Upon execution, the malware escalated privileges, moved laterally across systems, and deployed ransomware encrypting critical data across the network.

name: Supply Chain Compromise
description: Attack via compromised third-party software update or dependency.
text: A compromised software update introduced malware that installed a backdoor. The attacker established command and control communication, accessed sensitive data, and exfiltrated it.

name: Credential Stuffing Attack
description: Automated credential stuffing using leaked databases leading to account takeover.
text: An attacker used leaked credential databases to perform automated login attempts. After successfully compromising an account, they took it over, accessed sensitive data, and exfiltrated it.

name: Watering Hole Attack
description: Compromise of a trusted website to target specific users with drive-by downloads.
text: A frequently visited website was compromised to serve malicious content. When the target visited, a drive-by download executed code that stole credentials, enabling unauthorized access to sensitive data.

name: Zero-Day Exploitation
description: Exploitation of an unknown vulnerability for initial access and system compromise.
text: An attacker scanned for vulnerabilities and exploited a zero-day flaw. This allowed arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, and installation of a persistent backdoor for ongoing data exfiltration.
